function.description: Calculate the heat capacity at constant pressure of air using its temperature and volume. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Heat‑capacity of air at \(P=\text{const}\)**  

For an ideal gas the molar heat capacity at constant pressure (\(C_{p,\mathrm{m}}\)) does **not depend on the volume** – it depends only on the gas’s thermodynamic properties (composition, temperature, phase).  
At room temperature (≈ 300 K) dry air behaves essentially as a diatomic gas mixture whose ratio of specific heats \(\gamma=C_{p}/C_{v}\approx1.40\). Using this value:

\[
C_{p,\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\gamma\,R}{\gamma-1}
          =\frac{1.40\times 8.3145\;\text{J mol}^{-1}\!\!/\text{K}}
                 {1.40-1}=29.1\;\text{J mol}^{-1}\!\!/\text{K}.
\]

---

### Total heat capacity for your specified container

| Quantity | Symbol | Value |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Temperature | \(T\) | 298 K |
| Volume | \(V\) | 10 m³ |
| Pressure | \(P\) | 1 atm (= \(1.01325\times10^{5}\) Pa) *(assumed)* |

First find how many moles of air occupy the space:

\[
n=\frac{PV}{RT}
   =\frac{(1.01325\times10^{5}\,\text{Pa})(10\,\text{m}^3)}
           {(8.3145\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\!\!/\text{K})(298\,\text{K})}
   \approx 4.09\times10^{2}\;\text{mol}.
\]

Now multiply by the molar heat capacity:

\[
C_{p,\text{total}}
    = n\,C_{p,\mathrm{m}}
    =(4.09\times10^{2}\;\text{mol})
      (29.1\;\text{J mol}^{-1}\!\!/\text{K})
    \approx 1.19\times10^{4}\;\text{J/K}.
\]

> **Result:**  
> Under the stated conditions, the heat capacity of the air inside the 10 m³ vessel at constant pressure is approximately **\(1.2\times10^{4}\ \text{J K}^{-1}\)**.

*(If you need the value expressed per unit mass instead of per mole, let me know.)*
